The construct chain נַפְשׁוֹת עֶרְכּוֹ is recast as a head noun plus a relative clause; no clause stands in the Hebrew for *for whom* to subordinate, so the relative and its preposition are part of the rectum's own recasting (rule 46, closing paragraph) and carry the construct relation (rule 19). Head on *rated*, the English the ASV writes for the lexeme. Competing reading: *for whom* `added` under rule 2, rejected because rule 46 says such a relative is never added. Margin's literal gloss read and set aside (rule 38). Discontinuous around *each man* (rule 25).
The suffix refers to אִישׁ; ASV writes *each man* as subject and no possessive. *whom* points at the persons, not the man, so it is not the suffix's under rule 18.
No waw before כָּל; coordinator supplied (rule 14).

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'into the hands of them that did the work' is plural 'hands', matching the qere plural construct yede; the ketiv singular yad would read 'into the hand of'. The hebrew_gloss note ('brought it forth') is about a different word and does not bear on this unit.

ASV 'that had the oversight of the house' renders either the qere hophal participle ('those appointed over') or the unpointed ketiv hpqdym (qal 'overseers' or passive 'appointed ones'); the English does not distinguish active from passive here, and the only note (hebrew_gloss) concerns other wording.
